newsitem.title: USA: Cohen not first case of party Cabinet cross-overs.
newsitem.headline: Cohen not first case of party Cabinet cross-overs.

text.p: Republican William Cohen will be the first member of an opposition party to serve as defence secretary since Republican Robert McNamara had the job under Democratic presidents John Kennedy and Lyndon Johnson.

History shows it is unusual but by no means unprecedented for a president to make a Cabinet selection from the rival party. The last instance was believed to have been Republican Ronald Reagan's pick of Democrat Lauro Cavazos as education secretary.
Before that, Republican James Schlesinger, a defence secretary under Republican presidents Richard Nixon and Gerald Ford, went on to become energy secretary for Democratic President Jimmy Carter.

Henry Stimson may have prospered most of all in the rival party. A Republican, he was secretary of war under Republican Presidents William Howard Taft and secretary of state under Republican President Herbert Hoover.
He returned to the secretary of war position under Democratic presidents Franklin Roosevelt and Harry Truman.
Cohen was nominated Thursday for defence secretary by Democratic President Clinton. A Republican from Maine, he served 24 years in Congress.
